strengths: Addresses critical gap: First dataset combining semantic diversity (large scale, varied environments) with rich geometric annotations (camera poses, depth) at scale (2.7M clips, 7,089 hours)

Comprehensive multi-modal annotations: Geometric (per-frame poses and depth), semantic (structured captions at multiple levels), motion instructions with controlled vocabulary, dynamic masks, and hierarchical semantic tags

Thoughtful curation methodology: Manual screening for motion-rich content, empirical selection of MegaSaM over alternatives, novel spatial-aware caption generation using camera poses as geometric priors to correct VLM errors

Impressive scale and diversity: 21,000+ hours of raw video manually screened; covers diverse environments (urban, rural, indoor, waterfront, natural) and camera motions (walk, tour, drone, drive, train, boat); balanced SpatialVID-HQ subset

Rigorous analysis and clear presentation: Systematic comparison with Panda70M, novel camera motion metrics (MoveDist, RotAngle, TrajTurns), comprehensive statistics, well-designed visualizations of pipeline and dataset composition

Addresses real community need: Bridges long-standing divide between large semantic video datasets and small geometric datasets; well-suited for emerging world model and controllable video generation research
weaknesses: No downstream task validation: Paper claims improved model 'generalization and performance' (abstract, conclusion) without experimental evidence. Missing are baseline comparisons on video generation, 3D reconstruction, or camera control tasks—critical for demonstrating dataset value at top venues

Geometric annotation quality not validated: MegaSaM annotations are automatic with no ground-truth accuracy assessment. Paper acknowledges failures in 'extreme cases' and 'collinear motions' but provides no quantification. No sampling-based pose error analysis. Critical gap for a spatial dataset

Caption quality not systematically evaluated: LLM/VLM-generated captions lack manual verification or systematic quality metrics. Figure 9 shows one spatial correction example; insufficient evidence of systematic improvement. No user study on caption accuracy or spatial correctness

Incomplete technical documentation: Temporal smoothing filter details, motion instruction thresholds, filtering threshold justification (aesthetic >4.0, luminance [20,140], OCR <30%), and dynamic ratio computation underspecified. No ablation studies on design choices

Limited discussion of limitations: No quantification of MegaSaM failure rates in SpatialVID, no analysis of YouTube data representativeness or potential biases, computational costs barely mentioned, reproducibility concerns inadequately addressed (external model dependencies, YouTube availability)

Weak differentiation from concurrent work: Sekai dataset (concurrent, 600 hours with camera annotations) mentioned superficially; insufficient discussion of SpatialVID's unique advantages or why it's needed beyond existing alternatives like CameraBench and VLM4D

Motion instructions undervalidated: No evaluation of instruction quality, coverage, or alignment with camera trajectories. Keyboard representation (W,A,S,D) is simplistic and may not capture nuanced camera movements. No comparison with alternative representations

Dataset availability unclear: No mention of public release plans, license, or data sharing strategy. Dependency on external models (MegaSaM, Gemini, Qwen, SAM2) with versioning risks. No code release mentioned for annotation pipeline
